title: How the router learns which API groups each backend serves (aggregate vs forward)
answers: where does the router discover groups for aggregate apiservers
difference between aggregateBackend and forwardBackend in pkg/router
how are aggregate backends built from /apis
body:
Forward backends learn their group from their RouteBackend CR, so no active discovery call is needed.
Aggregate targets (baas_apiserver, cloud_app_platform_apiserver) have no CR. pkg/router/aggregate_discovery.go:discoverGroups actively polls <baseURL>/apis instead. It trims a trailing slash from the base URL so it never requests "//apis", and returns an error for non-200 responses.
The returned []metav1.APIGroup is filtered by matchesAnyPattern. newAggregateBackend then turns each group into an aggregateBackend, which proxies to the target's own host, in the same shape as forwardBackend.
Tests use an httptest server and live in pkg/router/aggregate_discovery_test.go (TestDiscoverGroups_*).
